purpose: Burn-in remediation experiment (W19). Single-factor change relative to mixak_canonical_config.json deep_refit: burn-in is increased from 50 to 20000 iterations. Cohorts, patients, windows, responses, seeds, retained sample count (keep=2000), thinning (thin=50), posterior-assignment rule and diagnostic thresholds are held identical so that any change in cluster stability is attributable to burn-in alone.
rationale: The archived executable pipeline and every revision refit used burn=50 with keep=2000 and thin=50, i.e. a 50-iteration burn-in preceding 100000 sampled iterations. A 50-iteration burn-in cannot be assumed adequate for a Bayesian mixture GLMM, so retained draws may include the transient from the initialization point. This profile tests whether the reported initialization sensitivity, degenerate low-prevalence components and high lag-1 autocorrelation are sampler-convergence artifacts rather than properties of the data. The chosen burn-in of 20000 iterations also exceeds the 5000-iteration burn-in described in the originally submitted Supplementary Methods.

converged_refit.scope: Deep multi-initialization re-estimation of K=2 versus K=3 and of every screening-depth CAUTION scenario under an adequate burn-in.
converged_refit.limitation: Each seed remains an independent single-chain initialization. Convergence is assessed per chain with the Geweke z diagnostic and effective sample size, and across the three aligned initializations with a post-relabelling split-chain R-hat computed on component means. Every prespecified seed, including degenerate or poorly mixing fits, remains in the denominator.

posterior_assignment.uncertainty_rule: 95% HPD lower bound for the selected component must exceed 0.5
